techniques.name: Straight Cut
techniques.definition: The most fundamental edit where one shot immediately replaces another without optical transitions or sound overlaps.
techniques.use_case: Standard dialogue, narrative progression, seamless continuity editing.
techniques.example: Cutting from a person looking left to what they are looking at on the right.

techniques.name: J-cut
techniques.definition: An edit where the audio of the upcoming shot precedes the visual cut (the viewer hears clip B before seeing clip B).
techniques.use_case: Smooth dialogue transitions, introducing new scenes fluidly without abrupt hard cuts.
techniques.example: Hearing a character start talking or a train whistle while still looking at the previous room.

techniques.name: L-cut
techniques.definition: An edit where the audio from the preceding shot continues playing over the visual cut into the next shot.
techniques.use_case: Showing reaction shots while speaker audio continues, creating emotional resonance.
techniques.example: Character A continues speaking while visual cuts to Character B's listening facial reaction.

techniques.name: Velocity Editing / Speed Ramping
techniques.definition: Dynamically changing playback speed within a single clip (e.g. fast-forwarding during movement, then slowing down to 100% or 25% at the point of action).
techniques.use_case: AMVs, montage edits, action sports, high-energy gaming or TikTok transitions.
techniques.example: Dancer jumping: clip speeds up 3x during spin, ramps to slow-motion (25%) at peak landing, then snaps back to normal speed.

techniques.name: Jump Cut
techniques.definition: A cut between two sequential shots of the same subject taken from almost identical camera angles.
techniques.use_case: Showing passage of time, high-energy YouTube/vlog edits, creating jarring urgency.
techniques.example: Vlogger speaking where pauses are trimmed out rapidly.

techniques.name: Match Cut
techniques.definition: A cut between two different objects, spaces, or compositions that match visually or action-wise.
techniques.use_case: Establishing thematic connection or seamless transition between scenes.
techniques.example: Cutting from a spinning bone thrown into the air to a spinning satellite in space.

techniques.name: Smash Cut
techniques.definition: An abrupt cut from an intense/loud scene to a tranquil/quiet scene (or vice versa).
techniques.use_case: Shock value, comedic timing, waking from a nightmare.
techniques.example: Cutting instantly from a roaring explosion to a peaceful alarm clock.

techniques.name: Invisible Cut
techniques.definition: An edit masked within motion or darkness (e.g., passing behind a pillar, camera whip, dark room transition) to give the illusion of a single continuous shot.
techniques.use_case: Onetake movie illusions (1917, Birdman), smooth music videos.
techniques.example: Camera follows actor behind a solid dark tree trunk, cutting to a new take on the other side.

techniques.name: Cutaway
techniques.definition: Cutting away from the main action to a brief shot of a related subject or detail before returning.
techniques.use_case: Providing context, hiding edits in dialogue, adding narrative detail.
techniques.example: Cutting to a ticking clock on the wall while two characters argue.

techniques.name: Cross-cutting / Parallel Editing
techniques.definition: Cutting back and forth between two or more events happening simultaneously in different locations.
techniques.use_case: Building suspense, drawing thematic parallels between two storylines.
techniques.example: Showing a detective racing to a location while cutting to the suspect preparing to flee.

techniques.name: Montage
techniques.definition: A series of short shots edited together to condense time, space, or information.
techniques.use_case: Training sequences, passage of years, travel highlights.
techniques.example: Showing an athlete practicing over months in a 30-second sequence set to music.

techniques.name: B-roll Insertion
techniques.definition: Overlaying supplemental or contextual footage over main interview/talking-head A-roll audio.
techniques.use_case: Illustrating points spoken by speaker, concealing jump cuts in dialogue.
techniques.example: Speaker mentions 'city traffic' and visual cuts to cars driving down Broadway.

techniques.name: Dialogue Editing & Audio Pre-laps
techniques.definition: Cleaning, balancing, and pacing spoken audio tracks between actors or speakers.
techniques.use_case: Ensuring smooth audio levels, removing room noise, and timing pauses for natural cadence.
techniques.example: Using room tone fill to smooth out background noise between dialogue takes.

techniques.name: Color Correction vs Color Grading
techniques.definition: Color correction balances exposure, white balance, and contrast. Color grading applies artistic color stylization (e.g. Teal & Orange, film stock emulations).
techniques.use_case: Establishing mood, matching shots from different cameras, creating cinematic looks.
techniques.example: Lowering color temperature for cool night shots, raising warmth for nostalgic golden hour look.
